task.name: Agent transport failures are recorded as story verdicts and persisted as adaptive learning signal
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

When an agent invocation fails at the transport layer — process exit=1 with a provider authentication error, no model output produced — the failure is converted into a story-level verdict and recorded as if a model had judged the work. Three phases each did this differently in a single run, and one of them wrote the result into the adaptive substrate as durable learning signal.

Sprint `45fee01e8027` (2026-07-26, issues 1947 and 1758) ran against a revoked Anthropic OAuth token. Every `claude` subprocess returned `exit=1: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token has been revoked.` No agent produced any output at any point. The run nonetheless proceeded for six minutes and produced verdicts:

**PREFLIGHT** failed for both stories and fell back to a PROCEED decision: `⚠ PREFLIGHT failed (exit=1) — no risk signals; fallback PROCEED (degraded)`, with the reason recorded as `Preflight agent failed (exit=1); no risk signals detected — falling back to conservative PROCEED.` The absence of risk signals is treated as evidence of low risk, when it is actually the absence of any analysis. "Conservative" here means proceeding.

**PLAN_REVIEW** converted the transport failure into a reviewer verdict: `✗ PLAN_REVIEW claude-opus failed (exit=1: ...revoked.) — treating as REJECT`, then `excluding claude-opus due to parse errors: Transport failure`. The reviewer pool silently shrank from three models to two and the sprint continued. A run whose review pool has lost a member to infrastructure failure is not comparable to one that completed with a full pool, but nothing downstream distinguishes them.

**DEV** produced the terminal outcome: `[DEV] FAIL | exit=1 | ... error output: Failed to authenticate` followed by `✗ ESCALATE Dev agent failed (exit=1) and produced no commits ahead of base — escalating to avoid an empty-diff APPROVE`. The escalation guard itself is correct — refusing to APPROVE an empty diff is right. The defect is the classification: this is recorded as ESCALATE, the outcome reserved for a story whose framing an agent found invalid, rather than as an infrastructure abort.

The consequence lands in the adaptive substrate: `[adaptive] escalation memory persisted via audit substrate: story=issue-1758 outcome=ESCALATE`. A revoked credential is now durable evidence that issue #1758 is a story that escalates, and that claude-opus rejects plans for it.

## Diagnosis

**Symptom:** Story #1758 reported `failed / ESCALATE` in live status with complexity 9, presenting as a story-quality problem. The actual cause was a dead OAuth token affecting every agent call in the run equally.

**Evidence:** `.forge/logs/issues-1947,1758/run-45fee01e8027.log` — the identical `401 OAuth access token has been revoked` string appears at lines 36, 51, 165, 192, and 326, spanning PREFLIGHT, PLAN_REVIEW, and DEV, across both stories. Line 195 is the ESCALATE, line 198 the adaptive persist.

**Ruled out — story-level cause.** No agent produced output in the entire run, so no model formed any judgment about either story. The token was already revoked at the first agent call (11:33:40), before any story-specific work began.

**Ruled out — duplicate of #1851 / #1852.** Those cover marking a run as tainted and filtering tainted runs out of consumption. This is upstream of both: the run is not currently recognized as tainted at all, because a transport failure is classified as a legitimate verdict at the point it occurs. Taint marking cannot filter what was never distinguished.

**Confirmed cause:** Each phase collapses a non-response into its own worst-case verdict — PROCEED for preflight, REJECT for review, ESCALATE for dev — without a category distinct from "an agent answered." Because those verdicts are indistinguishable downstream from real ones, the escalation path treats the result as story evidence and persists it.

**Fix-success criterion:** A run in which every agent invocation fails at the transport layer records no story-level verdicts and contributes nothing to adaptive memory. Given the log above as input, story #1758 does not appear in escalation memory, and the run is distinguishable from one where a dev agent ran and genuinely escalated.

## Expected behavior

A failure to obtain a model response must be a distinct category from a model response, everywhere a response is consumed. Process failure, authentication rejection, transport error, and timeout are all statements about the substrate rather than about the work, and the system must be able to say "no judgment was obtained" instead of substituting the most pessimistic judgment the phase can express. Substituting one is how an operator ends up reading a story-quality verdict that no agent ever formed.

This matters most where verdicts become durable. Evidence that outlives its run — adaptive routing memory, escalation history, reviewer reliability signal — must be sourced only from invocations that actually produced model output, because a verdict manufactured from an infrastructure failure is indistinguishable from a real one once written and will bias every later decision that reads it. The same reasoning applies to degraded-pool completions: a phase that lost participants to infrastructure failure has not produced a result of the same kind as one that completed intact, and the difference must survive into whatever consumes it.

handoff.summary:
Introduced a shared coordinator-level distinction between "a model judged the work" and
"no model answered", and threaded it through preflight, plan review, dev, adaptive
persistence, audit, and sprint reporting. New stdlib-only module
`src/theforge/coordinator/agent_failure.py` classifies an AgentResult that produced no
model output into auth / transport / timeout / startup / process categories; it treats
salvaged partial output, a tool trace, structured data, or a parsed handoff as positive
evidence a model spoke, and errs toward the pre-existing path for failure text it cannot
positively identify as a substrate event. New state fields: `agent_invocation_failures`
(every no-output invocation), `infrastructure_failure` (set only when the RUN's terminal
outcome is "no judgment obtained"), `degraded_pools` (pools that completed with members
lost to the substrate); `CoordinatorResult.infrastructure_failure` carries it to callers.
PREFLIGHT no longer writes PROCEED or BLOCKED when the agent produced nothing — it records
no verdict at all and ends the run as an infrastructure abort. PLAN_REVIEW records
NO_JUDGMENT plus pool-loss metadata instead of a manufactured reviewer REJECT, logs the
degraded pool when the minimum is still met, and aborts as infrastructure (not a plan
rejection) when every shortfall reviewer was silent. DEV's zero-commit guard still refuses
the empty diff but classifies a no-output failure as an infrastructure abort rather than
Phase.ESCALATE, and skips the escalation notification. `mark_infrastructure_abort()` writes
a FAILED `agent_judgment_obtained` trust check, so the existing ADR-0006 clause 4 gate
excludes the run from escalation history and model profiles; `_record_run_memory()`
additionally short-circuits with audit-visible logging. Audit record schema bumped 10 → 11
with a new top-level `agent_invocation` block and the matching reader-side migration;
preflight/plan_review audit blocks now render `NO_JUDGMENT` / `no_judgment` instead of being
dropped or defaulting to PROCEED, `run_end` emits `infrastructure_abort`, and the sprint
runner skips the `on_escalate` story-source callback for such runs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Absence of risk signals after a failed preflight is no longer treated as low risk.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The risk-signal fallback policy (#332) now runs only when the failed preflight salvaged model output; a silent preflight aborts before that branch.

story_deviations: No new Phase enum member. An infrastructure abort still terminates at Phase.ESCALATE; the distinction is carried by CoordinatorResult.infrastructure_failure, state.error_type, the taint marker, and the audit block. Adding Phase.INFRA_ABORT would have required matching changes to StoryOutcome, sprint outcome maps, status_reader failure sets, and RCA classifiers — well beyond the coordinator scope the story and preflight scoped. If the operator wants the sprint-level outcome string itself to read INFRA_ABORT, that is a follow-up.

Behavior change beyond the three named phases: preflight's conservative-PROCEED and risk-signal-BLOCKED fallbacks now require that the failed run produced some model output. Five existing tests in test_coord_preflight_fallback.py asserted the old contract on empty-output failures and were updated (with the salvaged-output helper preserving the original policy coverage, plus new no-output cases).

Audit shape: the preflight and plan_review audit blocks are now emitted when the phase ran but recorded no verdict/decision, rather than being dropped. This makes a no-judgment phase visible instead of looking like it never ran.

handoff.summary:
Iteration 2 is an advisory cleanup pass over the APPROVED iteration-1 implementation; no
redesign, two P2 fixes plus regression coverage.

(1) Tightened substrate-failure text matching in src/theforge/coordinator/agent_failure.py.
The bare numeric entries ("401", "403 forbidden", "429", "500 internal server error") were
matched by raw substring containment against the whole lowercased output, so ordinary agent
narration containing those digits — a line number, an issue reference, a loop count, a
timeout duration — would be classified as "no model output" and abort a run that a model had
in fact judged. HTTP status codes now match only in a code-shaped context: a status-ish word
immediately before the code (`API Error: 401`, `http 429`, `status_code=502`), or the code
immediately followed by its standard reason phrase (`503 service unavailable`). Recall that
the bare digits used to provide is carried by distinctive phrases added to the transport
list (`internal server error`, `servererror`, `bad gateway`, `service unavailable`,
`gateway timeout`). The broad `"api error"` phrase is tightened to `"api error:"`, the banner
form providers actually emit — verified against every occurrence in src/ and tests/, all of
which carry the colon. Both consumers (produced_model_output and classify_failure_category)
now route through new `_looks_like_auth_failure` / `_looks_like_transport_failure` helpers so
the phrase list and the code regex can never drift apart between the two call sites.

(2) Documented reachability in engine._record_run_memory(). PREFLIGHT and plan-flow terminal
outcomes return their phase result directly from run_task (the `_pf_result` / `_plan_result`
early returns), so those paths — including their infrastructure aborts — persist nothing by
omission; that predates #1951 and is unchanged by it. The docstring now states this and notes
that the infrastructure-abort guard IS load-bearing for the paths that do reach the function
(the DEV→VALIDATE→REVIEW loop, where the observed defect occurred, and both resume entry
points), so it is not read as dead code or deleted as unreachable. Routing plan-flow results
through the run tail was rejected as out of scope: it would change behavior for every plan
escalation, not just infrastructure aborts.

Added 13 parametrized regression cases to tests/test_coord_no_judgment_seam.py covering both
directions — digits in agent prose must stay model judgment, provider-context status codes
must still classify as auth/transport.

findings.description: _AUTH_PATTERNS and _TRANSPORT_PATTERNS include bare numeric substrings like '401', '403 forbidden', and '429', matched with plain substring containment against the full lowercased output text.

For a PREFLIGHT or PLAN_REVIEW infrastructure abort, run_task returns the phase's CoordinatorResult directly (if _pf_result is not None: return _pf_result / if _plan_result is not None: return _plan_result) before ever reaching _record_run_memory, so the new is_infrastructure_abort(state) early-return added to _record_run_memory is unreachable code on those two paths; the no-persistence outcome is achieved only because the function is never called at all, not because of the new taint check.

For a PREFLIGHT or PLAN_REVIEW infrastructure abort, run_task returns the phase's CoordinatorResult directly (if _pf_result is not None: return _pf_result / if _plan_result is not None: return _plan_result) before ever reaching _record_run_memory, so the new is_infrastructure_abort(state) early-return added to _record_run_memory is unreachable code on those two paths; the no-persistence outcome is achieved only because the function is never called at all, not because of the new taint check.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
